label: Elevated the Mencius into the canonical Four Books and grounded moral Principle in human nature
description: Zhu Xi canonized Mencius’s doctrine of innate moral sprouts as direct evidence that heavenly Principle (li) resides inherently within human nature (xing ji li).
dialecticalTension: Provides a cosmic metaphysical architecture for Mencian moral psychology.

label: Absorbed Buddhist metaphysical sophistication while refuting emptiness as nihilistic neglect of ethics
description: Zhu Xi transformed Confucianism by constructing a systematic metaphysics capable of rivaling Buddhism while attacking Buddhist monasticism for abandoning familial and civic duties.
dialecticalTension: Appropriates Buddhist speculative depth to defend world-affirming Confucian moral realism.

citations.author: Zhu Xi
citations.work: Zhuzi Yulei (Classified Conversations of Master Zhu)

label: Articulated the dual-aspect metaphysics of Li (normative Principle) and Qi (material force)
description: Zhu Xi’s li-qi polarity explained both universal moral order and concrete empirical diversity, shaping Chinese, Korean, and Japanese philosophy for centuries.
dialecticalTension: Balances transcendent moral coherence (li) with embodied psychophysical flux (qi).

citations.author: Zhu Xi
citations.work: Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsi Lu)

label: Provoked Wang Yangming’s Mind-School revolt against externalist "investigation of things"
description: After failing to attain sagehood by meditating on bamboo per Zhu Xi’s externalist method, Wang Yangming rejected Zhu Xi’s separation of mind and principle.
dialecticalTension: Generates the central Neo-Confucian schism between School of Principle (Lixue) and School of Mind (Xinxue).
